person: Nigerian first-time mother, day 6 after C-section, minimal overnight support
situation: It is 3 AM, the baby is finally asleep, and she needs to stand up from the bed to reach the baby
trigger: The moment of rising — the incision pulls and burns
context: Home after early discharge; hospital pamphlet gave only generic advice; alone at night
behaviour: holds the dresser and waits for the pain to pass

failed_attempts.why: it was the only guidance provided
failed_attempts.result: said only 'avoid strain and rest as needed'

constraint: No specific technique was ever given; reluctant to seek further medical contact over something she fears will be dismissed
thought: Maybe this is just what it feels like and I should cope
emotional_stake: Afraid something may be wrong internally, but reluctant to seek further medical contact over something she fears may be dismissed as normal
exact_language: I was scared to even stand up. Nobody warned me it would feel like that. I just held the dresser and waited for it to pass before I moved.
desired_change: To move — stand, sit, rise — without bracing in anticipatory fear of pain

evidence_source.excerpt: I was scared to even stand up.
